messages.text: also, is it normal for it to start mining as soon as given an ip?

Yes, that is normal. The B.04 boots straight into mining as soon as it has network. The firmware starts hashing on whatever pool config is already saved, so there is no "start" button to press.

Two things worth checking now:

1. Open the miner's web UI in a browser at its IP and look at the pool settings (stratum URL, worker name).
2. If the worker field is not your own wallet or account, the shares are going somewhere that is not you. Change it to your pool and your address, then save and let it restart.

Tell me what the pool and worker fields say and I will confirm you are set up right.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks, that tells me a lot. What I see on your screen:

- Thor OS, BC04, firmware 3.0.5 (20260909), board v1.2.0, chip BM1370
- Hashboard 50.4 C, VRM 58.8 C, fan 84% at 3404 RPM, all in safe range
- Uptime 6 minutes, so it booted and started hashing on its own, as expected
- Pool: solo.atlaspool.io port 3333, user ····

One question, and it matters given the broken seal: is that ···· address yours?

If it is not, the unit is solo mining to someone else's wallet, and you want to change it before it runs any longer. In that case go to the Pool tab, replace the user field with your own address plus a worker name (for example yourwallet.bc04), save, and let it restart.
nope, not mine.  thats a little disturbing

I agree, that is not how a sealed unit should arrive. Someone configured it to solo mine to their own wallet before it reached you.

Do this now, in order:

1. Set tab, factory reset. That wipes any saved pool, worker and network config, not just the one field you can see.
2. After it reboots, go to Pool and enter your own address plus a worker name, then save.
3. Check Set for a web UI password or access setting and change it if one is enabled.

Then send me a photo of the dashboard again and I will confirm it is clean.

I have passed the broken seal plus the foreign wallet to the team with the screenshot details, since that is a unit-handling issue, not a settings issue. They will confirm by email, usually within one business day. If you want a faster technical second opinion, JD (@nullhashrate) is on our Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf
also, its currently in overclock mode and I did not set that

That fits the same picture: the pool, the wallet and the clocks were all set by someone before you.

Two things:

1. Before you reset, grab a photo of the Set tab showing the frequency and core voltage values. That is the evidence of how hard it was being run, and it is gone after a factory reset.
2. Then do the factory reset. That puts frequency and voltage back to the stock BC04 profile along with the pool settings.

Good news on the hardware side: 50.4 C on the board and 58.8 C on the VRM are well inside safe range, so it was not being cooked while it ran that way. Nothing suggests damage so far.

Send me the Set tab photo and the dashboard after the reset, and I will check the stock clocks and hashrate look right.
